newsitem.title: USA: Solv-Ex says responds to lien filing.
newsitem.headline: Solv-Ex says responds to lien filing.

text.p: Solv-Ex Corp said Wednesday it has ended further work by Fort McKay Metis Corp of Alberta, Canada.
The company issued the statement in response to a lien filing from the Canadian construction company.
It said in a release that it has withheld payments to Fort McKay Metis pending resolution of billing complaints and said inferences that it is unable to pay its bills are "completely false."

Fort McKay Metis filed the lien for 3.8 million Canadian dollars, said Duane Iverson, the company's office manager. Iverson said the amount represents invoices through October 31, when Solv-Ex ended the relationship.
Solv-Ex Senior Vice President Herb Campbell said the company is withholding payment pending a detailed accounting analysis.

Solv-Ex is working on a project to produce crude oil from tar sands in Alberta, Canada. Last month its shareholders filed a class action suit alleging that certain Solv-Ex officers and directors misrepresented the company's business prospects.
Solv-Ex has said the suit is without merit and that it would fight it.

The company has the funds to complete its project in the first quarter 1997, Campbell said. It has hired more than 250 former employees of Fort McKay Metis and work will continue uninterrupted, the company officer said.
